responder.meaning: Upstream vocabulary with no round-trip headers. Either this was not proxied, or the header sanitizer removed the evidence of the round trip -- which would mean T-07's policy is destroying attribution. Both are worth knowing; neither is assumed.

0_upstream_existence.why_probed: Establishes whether the legacy MCP surface exists on this workspace at all. Governs the scope of everything below.
0_upstream_existence.consequence: The subject does NOT answer directly even with a full workspace credential, so there is no reachable legacy MCP surface on this workspace to expose. A 403 at the edge proves the POLICY FIRES but does not prove an exposure was closed, and a BROKEN deny would forward to a non-existent path and return a 404, which is also refusal-shaped. Attribution by responder is the only thing separating the two. NOTE: this caveat applies to M3's path only. Phase 2's unclaimed paths DO exist upstream and did answer 200 through the edge, so that half carries no such scoping.

which_control_answers_first.m3_is: a backstop, reachable only with the allow-list off
which_control_answers_first.why: Gravitee evaluates flows from the most GENERIC selector to the most specific. The allow-list's selector is `/` STARTS_WITH, the most generic there is, so it is evaluated FIRST however late it appears in the flows array. Proven both ways on 2026-10-21: with the allow-list enabled the MCP path answers in resource-filtering's words; disable that one flow and the same path returns M3's marker.
which_control_answers_first.consequence_accepted: AI-9. The caller receives the allow-list's reasonless 403 rather than M3's CONOPS reason. The trade is deliberate: the reason-carrier fails OPEN and the enforcer fails CLOSED, so the enforcer is the one that must answer first.

findings.b48: Gravitee FORWARDS any path that matches no flow selector; it does not refuse it. With this API's target at the workspace root, that made the AI route an open reverse proxy to the whole Databricks REST API for any caller holding ANY workspace token, on paths the route table never exposed. Measured 2026-10-21. Fixed on this API by a terminal resource-filtering whitelist derived from the forwarding flows' own selectors. SEVERITY CORRECTED IN PLACE (B-19): the first write-up of this finding said the paths were reachable with NO credential, as the gateway's injected identity. Measured: anonymous gets the upstream's 401, because the strip-and-inject steps live inside M1's flow, whose selector is EQUALS on the single model path. So this was a bypass of the ROUTE RESTRICTION, with the caller's own entitlements -- not a privilege escalation. It was one selector edit away from being one.
findings.ai_4: CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT, and it was real. M3's deny was policy-request-validation with an empty `rules` list, which validates nothing and passes everything. The policy LOADED and forwarded -- AI-4 predicted the outcome and the wrong mechanism. Re-expressed as a `mock` policy whose fields were read from this installation's schema endpoint, with enforcement moved behind it to the allow-list so a future failure of the deny falls CLOSED.
findings.what_caught_it: Not a gate and not the policy. This test, because it required Gravitee's own vocabulary instead of accepting any 4xx. An assertion of `status in (401, 403)` would have passed on the upstream's forwarded 401 and the no-op deny would have shipped as working.

scope_of_this_result: M3's path does not answer upstream even to a full workspace credential, so the M3 half is evidence that the CONTROL WORKS, not that a reachable exposure was closed. The unclaimed-path half carries no such caveat: those paths DO exist, DID answer 200 through the edge, and are now refused.

what_this_does_not_prove.the_estate: The allow-list is on this ONE API. scripts/29's sharing and storage APIs still forward unmatched paths and are confined only by their endpoint target carrying a deep base path, so a stray path appends and the upstream 404s -- confinement by string concatenation, not a control, and one target edit from being gone. Nothing here tests them. B-48 stays OPEN.
what_this_does_not_prove.authorisation: resource-filtering decides on the request PATH. It says nothing about who the caller is, and this route's plan is KEY_LESS (AI-1), so a 403 here is not an unentitled caller being refused.
what_this_does_not_prove.exhaustiveness: 3 paths were probed out of hundreds in the Databricks REST API. What makes the result general is the whitelist's default-deny SHAPE, not this sample.
what_this_does_not_prove.m2: Ungenerated (AI-5). §2.3.2 gives M2's method as 'MCP', a protocol not an HTTP method, and a POST-only selector would silently drop the streamable-HTTP event stream. OD-8's other half stays open.
what_this_does_not_prove.m3_as_first_responder: NOT shown, and cannot be while the perimeter is on: m3_is_first_responder=False. What is shown is that M3's mock fires, short-circuits and carries its reason when it is the control that is reached. A CONOPS claim that the caller is TOLD why the legacy MCP route is closed is therefore not supported by this run.
what_this_does_not_prove.step_conditions: AI-10. A step-level `condition` that does not evaluate true SILENTLY OMITS the policy -- PUT 200, deploy 202, no warning. Measured here by accident: a condition added to the allow-list step reopened /api/2.0/token/list to 200. Reverted and verified. No `condition` belongs on any step whose absence fails open.
what_this_does_not_prove.t15: No model path or credential injection was touched here -- but T-15 MUST be re-run, because the allow-list is now in the path of the model route T-15 measures.
